correctness.rationale: The hazards are explicit real-analytic functions with values in \((0,1)\) and sum identically to \(1\). Their cumulative hazards therefore sum to \(x\), giving an exact unit-exponential minimum. Alternating sine-sign intervals give explicit subsequences with \(R_i(x)/x	o0\), while opposite-sign intervals force \(R_i	o\infty\). The moment lower bound \(\mathbb E e^{\lambda X_i}\ge e^{\lambda x-R_i(x)}\) then proves heavy-tailedness for every \(\lambda>0\). Boundary/support and properness conditions were checked in the proof.

value.rationale: The recent literature makes segmentation the structural obstruction for heavy-tailed factors of a light-tailed minimum, while the canonical constructions are visibly interval-switched or piecewise. The explicit analytic example resolves a natural regularity question: segmentation does not require flat cumulative hazards, atoms, gaps, or discontinuous hazards. This is a structurally informative boundary statement rather than a parameter substitution or numerical recomputation.
